practice_name: Neem-turmeric paste for skin infections & wounds
science_check: Yes - study confirms documented antimicrobial use for skin infections/wounds
notes: From a 2025 study on herbal home remedies in Paniv, Maharashtra. Elderly women found to be the primary knowledge-holders; transmission mainly oral.

practice_name: Tulsi (holy basil) tea/leaves for cough, cold, stress relief
science_check: Yes - adaptogenic and immune-supporting properties documented in herbal/Ayurvedic literature
notes: Widely used household remedy; considered a revered plant in Ayurveda, grown in most homes.

practice_name: Reading ant behaviour (climbing higher, carrying eggs) to predict rain
science_check: Partially - ants are known to respond to humidity/pressure shifts, though this specific reading is unvalidated
notes: Farmers note ants climbing higher in long lines carrying eggs as a signal that rain is near.

practice_name: Red-wattled lapwing (Titwi) nest placement predicting monsoon timing
science_check: Unknown - anecdotal correlation, not scientifically tested
notes: Nest close to water = rain expected late; nest far from water = rain expected early with rising levels.

practice_name: Flame-of-the-Forest seed-pod position predicting monsoon rainfall pattern
science_check: Unknown - documented folk belief, not scientifically validated
notes: Seed position (bottom/middle/top of pod) read as indicating strong rain early/mid/late monsoon; documented by agri-scientist Dr K Ravi Shankar after 3 yrs fieldwork in AP.

practice_name: Flowering as monsoon-onset indicator
science_check: Partially - flowering cycles are known to correlate with seasonal temperature/moisture shifts
notes: Bahava blooms roughly 40 days before monsoon onset; used by local communities to time field preparation.

practice_name: Neem-leaf spray & fermented cow urine/buttermilk as organic pesticide
science_check: Yes - neem-based biopesticides and fermented mixtures are studied and confirmed to have pest-repellent effects
notes: Used before chemical pesticides existed; some farmers still integrate this with modern methods today.

practice_name: Gram Joshi / Panchang almanac reading for sowing dates
science_check: Unknown - based on astronomical/astrological calculation, not empirically tested
notes: Village astrologer reads annual rainfall/crop predictions from the Panchang during the Hindu New Year; farmers plan sowing around it.

practice_name: Sun-dried, salt-turmeric raw mango pickle (achaar) for long storage
science_check: Yes - salt, oil and acidic pickling environments are documented to inhibit microbial spoilage
notes: Raw mango cleaned, sun-dried, seasoned with salt/turmeric/oil (often mustard oil) for extended shelf life.

practice_name: Sandong - underground pit storage of vegetables
science_check: Yes - burying food below frost line and sealing with soil is a sound cold-storage method
notes: Trenches dug in gardens, filled with bagged vegetables, sealed with soil to protect from cold, damp and pests through winter.

practice_name: Salting and sun-drying fish for long-term storage
science_check: Yes - salting draws out moisture, inhibiting bacterial growth; well-documented preservation science
notes: Fish salted then dried under sun or in a ventilated area; can be stored for months depending on salting intensity.

practice_name: lost-wax metal casting
science_check: N/A - metallurgical craft skill, not a science-validation case
notes: Requires deep knowledge of metal alloys, fire management and sculptural skill built over decades; younger generations increasingly not learning it as economic viability drops.

practice_name: Natural dye extraction using alum (phitkari) as mordant
science_check: Yes - alum's role as a mordant in dye-fixing is chemically well understood
notes: Used by the Chhipa community in traditional hand block printing (Bagru); mineral-based mordant fixes natural dye colours onto cloth.

practice_name: Pattachitra scroll painting on cloth/palm leaf
science_check: N/A - traditional visual art craft, not a science-validation case
notes: Intricate scroll paintings depicting Mahabharata/Ramayana and Jagannath tales, created on cloth or dried palm leaves; techniques passed down strictly within family lineages.

practice_name: Ajwain (carom seed) water/steam for digestion and blocked nose
science_check: Yes - thymol in ajwain has documented antiseptic/decongestant and digestive properties
notes: Crushed ajwain with warm water for gas/indigestion; ajwain steam inhalation used to relieve nasal congestion.

practice_name: Idli/dosa batter fermentation
science_check: Yes — lactic acid bacteria fermentation improving digestibility/nutrition is well documented
notes: Rice+lentil batter naturally fermented overnight before steaming/cooking

practice_name: Copper engraving
science_check: N/A - traditional visual art craft, not a science-validation case
notes: Hand-engraved copperware (vessels, trays, decorative items) using traditional chisel-and-hammer techniques; motifs often drawn from Kashmiri floral and geometric design traditions passed down through family workshops

practice_name: Kani shawl weaving (hand-loom pashmina)
science_check: N/A - traditional visual art craft, not a science-validation case
notes: Uses fine pashmina wool woven on a wooden hand-loom using small wooden needles called "kanis" instead of a shuttle; a single shawl can take months to years to complete. Considered one of the most intricate and time-intensive weaving techniques in India.

practice_name: Walnut wood carving
science_check: N/A - traditional visual art craft, not a science-validation case
notes: Intricate hand-carving of walnut wood (grown locally in Kashmir) into furniture, panels and decorative pieces; valued for the wood's fine grain, which allows very detailed floral and jaali (lattice) patterns.

practice_name: Rogan painting — castor-oil paint craft
science_check: N/A - traditional visual art craft, not a science-validation case
notes: Thick paint made from boiled castor oil and vegetable dyes, applied to fabric using a metal rod rather than a brush. Once widespread in Kutch, now practiced by only a handful of families — one of the most acutely endangered crafts on this list.

practice_name: Kashmiri papier-mâché
science_check: N/A - traditional visual art craft, not a science-validation case
notes: Layered paper pulp moulded into decorative objects, then hand-painted with intricate floral/nature motifs. Political instability and cheap machine-made imitations have significantly reduced demand for the handmade version.

practice_name: wood-turning toy craft
science_check: N/A - traditional visual art craft, not a science-validation case
notes: Wood spun on a bow-driven spindle, shaped by hand, coloured with natural lac dyes. Artisan Boramma: learned from her father 20 years ago but does not want her daughters to pursue it due to low returns for the labour involved.

practice_name: Intercropping millets/pulses and maize/beans for soil health & pest control
science_check: Yes - intercropping's benefits for soil nitrogen and natural pest control are agronomically documented
notes: Farmers plant complementary crops together (e.g. millets with pulses) instead of monocropping to maintain soil fertility without chemical inputs.

practice_name: Clove oil for toothache and gum pain
science_check: Yes — eugenol in clove oil is a documented natural analgesic/antiseptic that numbs pain and reduces inflammation
notes: Clove oil applied directly, or a soaked cotton pellet placed near the affected tooth; long-standing Ayurvedic remedy

practice_name: Peacocks spreading feathers and dancing before rain
science_check: Unknown — widely observed but not scientifically confirmed as a rain predictor
notes: One of India's most recognisable monsoon folk-signs; peacocks are said to dance in the open just before a shower

practice_name: Garlic  and mustard oil paste for toothache
science_check: Yes — allicin in crushed garlic shown in small clinical trials to have antibacterial/anti-inflammatory effects comparable to clove oil
notes: Garlic crushed and mixed with mustard oil (sometimes with pepper), applied on cotton to the affected tooth for temporary pain relief

practice_name: Amla (Indian gooseberry) Murabba preserved in sugar syrup
science_check: Yes — high sugar concentration inhibiting microbial growth is a well-documented preservation method
notes: Tart amla fruit preserved whole in thick sugar syrup, extending shelf life through winter and making the sour fruit palatable year-round

practice_name: Fenugreek (methi) seeds/powder for  digestion
science_check: es — documented in Ayurvedic and modern nutrition literature for improving lactation, digestion, and cholesterol; used topically on wounds in some rural households
notes: Seeds soaked/powdered and taken with warm water or buttermilk; also mixed into cattle feed and applied to wounds/swellings in some regions

practice_name: Bawdi  (stepwell) water storage
science_check: Yes - stepwells provide reliable groundwater access year-round, engineering-validated
notes: Multi-story stepped structures (dating back to ~550 AD) allowing access to groundwater at varying depths as levels fluctuate seasonally; many now abandoned or filled in due to urban development

practice_name: Tanka (Underground rainwater storage tank)
science_check: Yes - documented as effective for potable rainwater storage in arid zones
notes: Underground cylindrical tanks built to store rainwater collected from rooftops/courtyards for household drinking use through dry months; traditionally maintained by desert communities

practice_name: Kund (saucer-shaped rainwater catchment well)
science_check: Yes - functional rainwater harvesting design still referenced in modern water-conservation planning
notes: Saucer-shaped catchment area sloping toward a central underground well, historically lime-and-ash lined for purification; earliest known examples date to 1607 AD, many now replaced with plain cement construction losing traditional building knowledge

practice_name: Floodplain water harvesting system
science_check: Yes - documented as an effective indigenous flood-irrigation system for paddy cultivation
notes: Ahars (catchment basins) connected to pynes (diversion channels) that capture monsoon floodwater from rivers for paddy cultivation; system has significantly declined due to unmaintained channels and shifting land-use patterns
